directAnswer: St. Silverius, son of Pope Hormisdas, was pope from 536 until he was deposed in March 537. Caught between the Goths and the Byzantine general Belisarius, he was accused of treason, removed from office, and sent into exile, where he died. He is venerated as a martyr, with a feast day of June 20.

paras: Silverius was a subdeacon when the Ostrogothic king Theodahad pressed for his election in June 536 after Agapetus died in Constantinople. His father, Hormisdas, had been pope before him, having married before ordination.

Within months, the Byzantine general Belisarius entered Rome in December 536, and the city was soon besieged by the new Gothic king, Witiges. Silverius found himself in a city occupied by imperial forces while the empress Theodora pursued her own aims for the papacy.

Theodora wanted the deposed Patriarch Anthimus restored and favored the deacon Vigilius, who was then in Constantinople, as a more pliable pope. In March 537 Silverius was accused of corresponding with the Goths to betray the city; the Liber Pontificalis says the letters were forged. Belisarius stripped him of his office and sent him to Patara in Lycia.

The local bishop protested to Justinian, who ordered an inquiry and sent Silverius back to Italy. Vigilius, now installed as pope, had him taken to the island of Palmarola in the Pontine group, where he died later in 537, by tradition from starvation. He is honored as a martyr and as patron of the island of Ponza.

keyFacts: Pope from June 536 until deposed around March 537
Accused of treason and deposed by the general Belisarius
Died in exile on the island of Palmarola in 537
Venerated as a martyr; feast day June 20

faqs.question: Why was Pope Silverius deposed?
faqs.answer: He was accused of plotting to hand Rome to the besieging Goths. Ancient sources say the letters used as evidence were forged, and the empress Theodora wanted Vigilius in his place.

faqs.question: Was Pope Silverius the son of a pope?
faqs.answer: Yes. His father was Pope St. Hormisdas, who had married before entering the clergy. Silverius was born before his father's ordination.
